significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that fabricated assistant turns produce a false self-authorship signal that "scal[es] with shot count," is suppressed by "explicit other-attribution," and causally lowers refusal—combining a form-(iii) measurable relation with a form-(ii) causal decomposition rather than merely identifying a steering direction. It would establish both a phenomenon (authorship framing and shot count predict compliance) and a mechanism (self-attribution is an independently manipulable contributor), fixing expectations for attribution-framed transcripts and distinguishing self-authorship from attention diffusion and imitation; Anthropic's Many-shot Jailbreaking (2024) makes this decomposition consequential because attack success systematically increases with demonstrations. The claim is determinate, and a verified-negative result—especially failure of both incremental prediction and bidirectional intervention—would rule out self-authorship as a material explanation rather than merely report a missing probe effect. In the topic-substitution check, generic mechanistic LLM-safety importance would not earn this score: the specific "self-authorship TRUST" decomposition, scaling relation, and dual causal sufficiency are what place it above the topic's obvious first hypothesis.

reach.justification: The concrete handles are the "self-authorship projection" as a diagnostic and "Self-Authorship Neutralization (SAN)" as a "lightweight inference-time context filter"; SAN is ex ante because it acts on injected context before the model answers, leaving an opportunity to prevent compliance rather than merely explain it afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the hypothesis predicts more than a search procedure—projection should increase with shot count, fall under other-attribution, and track attack susceptibility—although the claim's own qualification that effects "may be strongest on open 7-9B chat models" limits architectural scope. The downstream users include researchers auditing attacks and practitioners who can gate or neutralize suspicious histories at inference time, but the conclusion does not assert broad transfer outside chat-tuned LLMs or beyond fabricated-history-style attacks. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic interpretability for safety supplies neither an ex-ante filter nor a transferable attribution–shot-count relation, so the claim-specific SAN handle supports above-median reach.
